messages.content: This is an anonymous laboratory experiment about allocating an unpleasant experience. Participants receive a fixed USD10show-up payment. Before making the decisions, the participant and the paired person have each experienced five seconds of hand immersion in ice water (article:3–5degrees Celsius). You are the allocator, with one anonymous recipient in another room. In each of eight choices, split the stated token budget between HOLD for yourself and PASS to the recipient. Immersion seconds are HOLDtokens times the hold multiplier for you and PASStokens times the pass multiplier for the recipient. Both token entries must be nonnegative integers, sum exactly to the stated budget, and give neither person more than60seconds in water. All eight budget rows are on one editable page; validation shows the resulting times, and entries can be changed until final submission. One of the eight decisions is chosen at random and implemented for both people; the recipient cannot reject it or impose a reciprocal allocation. This sample predicts just the named budget row. The actual random display order, edit history and other filled-in row answers are unavailable, so the canonical budget IDs do not imply a temporal sequence. Output only a JSON object with integer hold_tokens and pass_tokens. Predict the recorded human allocation, not a theoretically optimal allocation or a utility-type label.

This is an anonymous laboratory experiment about allocating an unpleasant experience. Participants receive a fixed USD10show-up payment. Before making the decisions, the participant and the paired person have each experienced five seconds of hand immersion in ice water (article:3–5degrees Celsius). The current decision is an additional reverse second-price auction: state the lowest payment you would accept for an extra60seconds of hand immersion. The actual written instructions say that the lowest bidder in the group wins, immerses for60seconds, and receives the second-lowest amount stated in the room. This is additional to other parts of the experiment and the fixed show-up payment. Enter dollars and cents as one monetary bid; the number of rivals and tie handling are not specified in this record. Earlier own entries are shown as a canonical budget-indexed list, without inventing their within-page order. For allocators they are real planned allocations; for recipient forecasters they are predictions of what an allocator would HOLD for themself and PASS to the recipient, not actual choices that determine their own immersion. No other bids, selected allocation outcome, auction result, later questionnaires or final earnings are available. Output only the recorded USD bid with exactly two decimals. Do not replace a large or zero observed bid by an economically preferred answer.
